guidance: Zone captions on entry ("Switchbacks - North Side", "Lighthouse Courtyard", "Rooftop - North Side") name areas so text directions work (LP4 1:00:09, 1:01:27; LP34 1:28:45; PS34).
The flythrough shows the tape beside a ruined wall with a pipe and the bay (LP34 1:23:02), the same view the player gets when leaving the left window.
The water tower is a skyline landmark from the yard and the switchbacks (LP34 1:28:39-1:28:42).
Closed doors with a guard are shown in the flythrough (LP34 1:22:56) and sit beside the courtyard the letter line uses, so the lock is seen long before the key.
Inside the cell block, light through the two open windows at the end of the top tier draws the eye; the tape is visible through the left one (LP34 1:29:05).
Bins carry their own text feedback ("1 of 5 ... no cellblock keys here!", LP34 1:24:08), so the search has a visible counter.
Hidden on purpose: the cell-block interior, the tank interior, the south-rooftop loop, the tall tower platform.
designLogic: The remake gates the tape behind another goal (Release the Prisoner): the tape is the reward for opening the level's biggest locked building, and its route uses that building once.
The search goal (5 bins) is spread across the island, so by the time the cell block opens the player knows the island; the tape then needs only ≈ 30 s.
Inside-out route: climb a closed interior (tiers, spiral stairs) and exit through a window to the outside landmark. It reverses the usual outside-in climb and gives a dramatic reveal of the bay.
The water tower is the island's secret-holder in every version: PS1 tape on its roof, PS2 pro spine into its open tank, remake spine goal plus tape beside it.
Height comes from the island itself: the tape is "high" because the cell block sits on the summit; no extra structure was needed.

Letters stay on one readable line in the remake (one rail for S-K-A, a slope jump, a QP), whereas the original spreads them down the hill; the remake keeps the teaching letters simple and moves the challenge to the tape.
Falling into the bay is the main failure (LP4 "You big drip!"); routes near the shore are low-cost practice, routes on the summit cost a climb.
PS1 relies on portals (to the cell-block roof) and a warp link (VG) to make a tall island navigable on weaker hardware; the remake replaces them with opened doors and roof captions.
Pro COMBO in the original ends by flying through a window, the same move the remake tape uses: a late-career original idea became the remake's tape.
Remake runs are 10:00; LP34 used ≈ 4:50 for every regular goal including the gated tape (1:23:08 → 1:29:10).
remakeChanges: Tape: none in the PS2 career; PS1 put it on the water-tower roof via a kicker-rail from the cell-block roof (CC1); the remake puts it outside the cell block's top-tier window above the water tower, behind Release the Prisoner (PS34; LP34).
Find the Guard's Keys (16 keys) and Distract the Guards (bins) merge into Release the Prisoner (5 bins with a key) (THG vs PS34).
Semi Flip the Bulldozer becomes a pro Sal Flip over the Bulldozer; a Double Heelflip of the Massive Crumbling Stairset reuses the original gap name (THG gap list vs PS34).
Rune Glifberg's water-tower spine (original pro challenge step) becomes a regular goal "Spine Transfer into the Water Tower" with a drain-the-pool valve (THG vs PS34).
Take the Alcatraz Tour (skitch) becomes Listen to Ranger Ron's Story (skitch for ≈ 20 s); Bullseye Launch's target returns as the IG-logo target (THG vs PS34).
S-K-A-T-E moves from a hill-descending run (original) to one rail line in Lighthouse Courtyard (remake).
transfer: Gated crystal: lock a tall building with a door that a search goal (five bins, last one holds a key) opens; put the crystal just outside an upper window of that building, so the route is interior climb → window → rail → jump. Use a travelling-rail-free static rail out of the window; our grind ollie (≈ 2.4 m pop) clears the crystal height above the rail.
Inside-out climb: interior quarter pipes and a spiral handrail up three tiers (≈ 3-4 m each) give vert air and grind practice in a closed room before the exposed exit.
Landmark cable network: hang several cables from a water tower to roofs and walls (PS1 layout), then put lesser collectibles on the cables and the crystal at the tank.
Spine into a tank: a drained pool beside a tower whose tank has an open top; spine transfer from the pool rim into the tank (our spine transfer works pipe to pipe).
Make failure geographic: put early collectibles near the shore (cheap water reset) and the crystal on the summit (costly climb), so difficulty rises with altitude.
Caption zones on entry so directions in hints can name them, as the remake does.
openQuestions: Whether the remake tape can be reached from outside without releasing the prisoner (HardcoreGamer says "theoretically"; no route documented).
Exact interior route LP34 used to get from the floor to the top tier (frames at 1 s show a ride up the halfpipe and a steep rail view; could be the spiral stair rail).
Original PS2 water tower: THG calls it a "watchtower" in Rune's challenge; the gap list says "water tower"; treated as the same structure.
Meaning of the VG "WARP" line and PS1 "SWITCH" goal (CC1 does not mention them).
